{{distinguish|Rogers polynomials}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''Rogers–Szegő polynomials''' are a family of [[orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle]] introduced by [[Gábor Szegő]],{{sfnp|Szegő|1926}} who was inspired by the [[continuous q-Hermite polynomials|continuous ''q''-Hermite polynomials]] studied by [[Leonard James Rogers]]. They are given by
:<math>h_n(x;q) = \sum_{k=0}^n\frac{(q;q)_n}{(q;q)_k(q;q)_{n-k}}x^k,</math>
where <math>(q;q)_n</math> is the descending [[q-Pochhammer symbol|''q''-Pochhammer symbol]]. The Rogers-Szegő polynomials satisfy the recurrence relation{{sfnp|Vinroot|2012}}
:<math>h_{n+1}(x;q) = (1+x)h_n(x;q) + x(q^n-1)h_{n-1}(x;q)</math>
with <math>h_0(x;q)=1</math> and <math>h_1(x;q)=1+x</math>.
